Traditional Irish Butter for Imbolc Eve

Served at: Imbolc Eve (La Fheile Bride)

About 1 cup (240 ml) of butterPrep 10 min

Butter holds a special place in Irish tradition, especially during Imbolc Eve (La Fhéile Bríde), which celebrates the beginning of spring and honors St. Brigid. Making fresh butter at home is a simple yet meaningful way to connect with the festival's themes of renewal and abundance.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (480 ml) heavy cream, chilled
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt (optional)

Method

  1. Pour the chilled heavy cream into a large mixing bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer.
  2. Beat the cream on medium-high speed for about 5-7 minutes. First, it will turn into whipped cream, then it will begin to separate into butter and buttermilk.
  3. Once the butter solids clump together and separate from the liquid, stop mixing.
  4. Strain the mixture through a fine mesh strainer or cheesecloth to separate the buttermilk from the butter.
  5. Gather the butter into a ball and rinse it under cold water, kneading gently to remove any remaining buttermilk.
  6. If desired, sprinkle salt over the butter and knead it in evenly.
  7. Shape the butter into a block or place it in a container and refrigerate until firm.

Tips

  • Use fresh, high-quality cream for the best flavor and texture.
  • Save the buttermilk for baking or cooking—it adds a lovely tang to breads and pancakes.
  • For a festive touch, mix in fresh herbs like chives or parsley before shaping the butter.
